gemini-2.5-flash.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate experienced a gross prior year reserve strengthening of GBP 27.071 million in 2016, representing 14.19% of its opening gross claims outstanding. This adverse development was primarily driven by a deterioration in the 2013 and prior years of account, particularly within the professional indemnity, Directors and Officers, and medical malpractice classes of business. The 2014 and 2015 years of account also saw increased loss ratios. Causes included a significant increase in incurred claims, the materialisation of large losses, late reporting on personal accident claims, and the incorporation of large loss loads and reserve increases advised by independent claims consultants following a comprehensive review of open claims. The Managing Agent's decision to put the Syndicate into run-off for 2017 also contributed to the need for increased unexpired risk provisions and a re-evaluation of reserves.

gpt-5-mini.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding and prior-year gross movement taken from Note 17 (Technical provisions) 'Balance at 1 January' and 'Changes for prior years' (explicit gross figures). Some LOB-specific movements are reported only net or narratively; gross LOB-level movements are partially inferred from textual amounts (e.g. GBP 16.5m gross increase for professional indemnity, GBP 3.2m for personal accident). Named-event granularity is limited (no specific catastrophe names). Where only net figures were presented in narrative, gross equivalents were taken from actuarial commentary where available; otherwise amounts left null or assigned lower confidence.
